newsitem.title: UK: Small slip could set off San Andreas, experts say.
newsitem.headline: Small slip could set off San Andreas, experts say.

text.p: Tiny changes in a cycle of small slips could set off "the big one" along California's quake-prone San Andreas fault, geologists reported on Wednesday.

Mathematical models show that the cycle of stress and release along the fault "could trigger major earthquakes", Chi-yeun Wang of the University of California at Berkeley and Yongen Cai of Peking University in Beijing said.
"The San Andreas fault may be in a critical state and sensitive to small perturbations in regional compression," they wrote in a report in the science journal Nature.

The fault marks where two huge tectonic plates -- enormous slabs of rock that float on the earth's surface -- rub together. Quakes are associated with the build-up and release of pressure caused by this rubbing.

Wang and Cai ran a series of mathematical simulations of the process and found small increases in pressure could "lock" the fault, making earthquakes less likely, while small decreases in compression could release the locked part and allow earthquakes to happen.
They said their theories could be checked using Global Positioning System (GPS) satellite data, which constantly measure points on the earth's surface.
